critique: The note proves the advertised two-sided unequal-information minimax rate in the stated shared-population discrete model; the headline is not resting on a conjecture or a one-sided surrogate. Its main limitation is scope: this is a specialized extension of the supervised discrete-ATE frontier rather than a broadly reusable framework or resolution of a recognized field-wide problem. The interpretation as a chart-review allocation decision rule exceeds what the theorem directly supplies, because the risk constants remain existential and the note provides neither usable finite-sample calibration nor a cost-based allocation analysis. Those limitations constrain leading-journal significance and practical impact but do not reduce the matched minimax theorem below a field-level contribution.
